title: The Krull dimension of a ring is the supremum of the heights of its primes
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ let $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p\in\{0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$ be the supremum of the integers $t\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_t$ of prime ideals of $R$ with $\mathfrak p_t\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Then the Krull dimension of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] is
$$
\dim R=\sup_{\mathfrak p\subset R\ \text{prime}}\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\},
$$
the supremum of the empty family being $-\infty$ (the case $R=0$).
